magicGroundDelivery.text: One runtime decal overlay for all magic ground (generated variants and live mutations). No school terrain layers in the template.
evidence: Entity-less scene decals render over generated relief (run 23716 d1: 16 decals across the hill flank, 48% of their boxes changed).
SetFactor1 tints a vanilla decal material per instance (run 6284 v3: 1,610 sampled magenta pixels), so one published stamp set can carry several schools.
Creation and removal are cheap: 7,500 decals in 4.3 ms, removed in 4.7 ms, re-created identically (run 23716 recreated200 vs count200).
Frame time held the 60 fps cap with 7,500 decals in view (p95 17.6 ms); main-thread cost is about 0.36 us per decal per frame (0.46 ms at 0, 3.19 ms at 7,500).
B does not fit the 15-slot budget: 8 school layers beside 9-10 biome layers exceed 15, and baked layers cannot change at run time, so mutations need decals anyway.
conditions: Runtime-made textures do not render on decals (Material.CreateCopy + SetTexture(DiffuseMap, Texture.CreateFromByteArray) drew nothing, with or without CheckAndRegisterToDecalSet). MMR-259's school textures must be published as module decal materials (precedent: NavalDLC's own decal_water_foam, created at run time with Material.GetFromResource).
Keep the in-view total under about 5,000 decals (about 2 ms of main thread); stamp about one decal per source cell (world A: 1,784 mutated land cells).

decalTechnique.text: decal = Decal.CreateDecal(null); decal.SetMaterial(Material.GetFromResource(<published decal material>)); scene.AddDecalInstance(decal, "editor_set", true); decal.SetIsVisible(true); decal.SetVectorArgument(atlas scale u, scale v, offset u, offset v); decal.Frame = <world frame whose rotation columns are scaled by the half extents; box [-1,1]^3, projected along local z>; optional decal.SetFactor1(ARGB tint). Remove with scene.RemoveDecalInstance(decal, "editor_set"). Scene created with DecalAtlasGroup.Worldmap (as SandBox.MapScene).
rejected: GameEntity + AddComponent(Decal) renders only after decal.CheckAndRegisterToDecalSet() (run 23716 d3 drew nothing; run 6284 v4 with the call drew). Usable, but an entity per decal buys nothing.
Mesh decal fallback (Mesh.CreateMeshWithMaterial(decal material) on a [-1,1]^3 box): drew nothing (run 23716 d4).
Runtime textures on a material copy: drew nothing (run 23716 d2, run 6284 v1). Material.CreateCopy alone works (run 6284 v2).

terrain513.text: Level-7 terrain (513 samples, 4 x 4 nodes of 128 cells) written by our encoder (tools/scenebin/terrain_bin.py) reads in 0.13 s, is ready in 0.9 s with the same shader work as level 6, renders without seams or artefacts, and holds the 60 fps cap with main-thread time equal to level 6 (0.52 vs 0.52 ms at the mountain view). terrain.bin 302 KB.
terrain513.caveat: GPU cost above the 60 fps cap is unmeasured on this machine; the C++ surface encoder still caps at 64 cells per node and must be extended by MMR-278.

mapTrees.text: Map trees placed through flora.bin render: 88,000 instances (map_spruce_mix, worldmap_tree_beech_01, worldmap_tree_acacia_01; scale 0.18-0.32) loaded (Scene.GetFloraInstanceCount 88,000), read well at camera distance 38, and fade with distance per the kind's view_distance. Frame time held the cap; the overview costs about 0.24 ms more main thread than the same scene without trees.
mapTrees.format: FLR2: u32 payload bytes, u32 count, then per tree u32 name length, name, u32 flora_variation index, 16 f32 (rows: rotation x scale, then x y z 1), 4 f32 colour (1,1,1,1). Read from the installed Main_map flora.bin (69,500 trees) and written by tools/scenebin/build_probe_slots.py flora_bin().

1_layers.compositing: Alpha-over, front to back from slot 15 down to slot 0 (slot 0 opaque), linear in the stored weight: the measured ratio is affine in w with residual under 1.5% (band A, plain colour ramp) and a higher slot fully covers a lower one (band B: green at w = 0.5 over the magenta ramp keeps green constant to 0.4%, magenta enters at half strength). The shader divides by smooth_blend_amount (1.0 here). Weights at or below 2/255 draw nothing (shader threshold 0.01).
1_layers.heightBlend: Only with use_transparency_of_ground_slope = true: the layer stays invisible until w is about 0.6 and then rises steeply to full at w = 1 (band C). Without the flag the ramp is linear (band D). MMR-255: leave the flag off and convert target fractions with the over-compositing inverse a_k = f_k / (f_0 + ... + f_k).
1_layers.perSeasonMasks: Inert in practice: MBMapScene.SetSeasonTimeFactor(1) and Scene.SetWinterTimeFactor(1) produced byte-identical images, so neither the per-season node masks (layer 1 removed from the winter mask in half the nodes) nor the per-season layer variants switch at run time. Write identical masks and identical variants for all four seasons; the seasonal look has to come from dynamic snow.
1_layers.loadAndCompile: Scene.Read 0.04-0.17 s; ready to render about 1 s after Read for 2, 6 and 15 layers per node and for level 6 and level 7. Each scene compiles its own terrain shader (6-9 pbr_terrain / pbr_terrain_gbuffer permutations, 'Missing shader from sack' then compile_shader in the engine log), finished inside that second.
1_layers.frameCost: Every view held the 60 fps cap (mean 16.67 ms, p95 at most 17.9 ms) for 2, 6 and 15 layers per node. The cap is outside the game's settings (docs/first-test-profile.md); Utilities.SetForceVsync(false) did not lift it, so GPU cost above the cap is unmeasured. Main-thread time per frame: 0.39-0.56 ms for 2, 6 and 15 layers (no layer-count trend).

2_scale.tileSize: A layer's scale is its tile size in map units: scale 5 repeats every 5.03 units, scale 20 every 20.0 units (top-down autocorrelation in x and y).
2_scale.pxPerUnitAt38: 37.0 px per map unit at the screen centre on the 1,024-px-tall probe window (vertical FOV 0.698 rad, distance 38, elevation 0.635 rad); in general 0.0362 x screen height per unit, about 39 at 1080p. The camera model matches the measured tile periods to under 1%.
2_scale.guidance: At distance 38 the screen spans about 58 x 37 units. Scale 5 reads as uniform noise; scale 15-20 shows the texture with 2-4 repeats across the screen. A 2048 texture at scale 20 gives about 100 texels per unit against 37 screen px: identity must come from macro colour, not detail inside the tile.

answers.3_decals: See decisions.decalTechnique and decisions.magicGroundDelivery. Entity-less path decals follow relief (hill flank, slopes up to about 40 degrees). Cost: 200 / 1,000 / 3,000 / 7,500 decals in view all held the cap; main-thread time 0.46 / 0.84 / 1.59 / 3.19 ms. Removal returns the image exactly to the decal-free baseline; re-creation reproduces the earlier image.

4_dynamicSnow.flag: use_dynamic_weather_effects="true" alone does nothing visible. With dynamic_flowmap_texture_name="main_map_snow_flowmap" (vanilla Main_map's pair) the terrain snows from that texture.
4_dynamicSnow.seasonResponse: MBMapScene.SetTerrainDynamicParams(scene, (x, 0.65, 0)) drives the season threshold on the application thread: x = 0.55 (summer) against x = -0.1 (winter) changes the four quadrants by 7-55 grey levels; the shader's grad = smoothstep(x - 0.65, x + 0.65, R).
4_dynamicSnow.setDynamicSnowTexture: Scene.SetDynamicSnowTexture after Read has no visible effect (runtime RGBA pattern in R, G or A, a B water mask, and the vanilla main_map_snow_flowmap all gave identical images). Calling it before Read hangs the engine (run 26296). The shader samples the terrain's dynamic texture with v = 1 - y / size, R = snow threshold, B = water mask (source: terrain_pixel_functions.rsh).
4_dynamicSnow.channelAndOrientation: Not settled in game: no runtime pattern reached the shader. By shader source: R channel, texture row 0 at the north edge (max y), column 0 at x = 0. The vanilla texture's snow lands mostly in the two northern quadrants of our terrain, consistent with row 0 = north.
4_dynamicSnow.templateWinterGrass: Does not whiten the map: the template's winter grass variant (snow_b_d) never activates (see 1_layers.perSeasonMasks).
4_dynamicSnow.colorGradeManager: A runtime MapColorGradeManager (GameEntity.CreateAndAddScriptComponent) hangs the engine in a non-map scene (run 23716; not responding, no CPU). Drive SetTerrainDynamicParams from our own per-tick code instead.
4_dynamicSnow.renderVersion: terrain_render_version="1" never reached ready to render (run 6284 hung in load). Do not set it.
4_dynamicSnow.openForMMR256: A per-world snow mask needs a texture the terrain resolves by name at Read. Untested: registering a runtime texture by name (Texture.LoadTextureFromPath before Read; run 26296 hung on the earlier variant before reaching it). MMR-256 must prove that route in the acceptance build or fall back (permanent-white layer only, plus SetTerrainDynamicParams with no seasonal mask).

5_tints.mode1: Adds the colour to the layer albedo (desert_floor_a + (0.2, 0, 0): +0.075 linear red after lighting, other channels unchanged).
5_tints.mode2: Multiplies and saturates, so it only darkens ((1, 0.55, 0.55): lit ratios 1.00 / 0.70 / 0.72 with fog diluting).
5_tints.fullColourTextures: The full-colour battle textures read as their biome at map scale (desert_floor_a, desert_floor_c_d, ground_drygrass_a_d, forest_a_d, ground_mud_b_d, ground_beach_a_d, ground_nord_grass_a_d, rock_k_d, ice_a_d, snow_a_d). The *_mainmap textures (ground_grass_b_d_mainmap, ground_forest_b_d_main_map, main_map_mountains_d) are pale and blue-white without the vista colour multiply and should not be used as plain biome layers.

6_terrainResolutionAndNormals.normals: Normals from a [1,2,1]/4 x2 smoothed field are indistinguishable from Sobel on the raw field at level 6 (Laplacian energy 5.23 vs 5.23 on the oblique mountain view): the facets and spikes come from geometry, not from normals.
6_terrainResolutionAndNormals.shapedField: The shaped, half-vertical-scale level-7 field (150 samples despiked, masked [1,4,1]/6 low-pass) renders without spikes or blade ridges; land slope p95 39.6 degrees against 62.6 for the unshaped level 7 and 69.0 for today's level 6 (build/probe-slots/probe-slots.json worldA).
